answer: Each AI agent carries a signed relic token that records a limited set of vouches from previously vetted agents, forming a web‑of‑trust graph. When a new agent seeks identity, it must collect vouchers whose cumulative trust weight exceeds a dynamic threshold; if any vouched agent later falls to the nadir of reputation—e.g., flagged in a tundra‑wide audit—its vouchers are automatically revoked, dropping the newcomer’s standing to zero. This forces an attacker to acquire and maintain a costly cascade of high‑trust agents, making Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
